title: Tanvir's New Routine
story: Tanvir, 24, has moved from Sylhet to Dhaka for his first job at a software company in Gulshan. He shares a small flat in Mohammadpur with his school friend Imran, a young doctor who often works night shifts. Long commutes, late nights and new responsibilities are slowly changing his routine.
storyBn: ২৪ বছরের তানভীর প্রথম চাকরির জন্য সিলেট থেকে ঢাকায় এসেছে; সে গুলশানের একটি সফটওয়্যার কোম্পানিতে কাজ করে। মোহাম্মদপুরের একটি ছোট ফ্ল্যাটে সে স্কুলের বন্ধু ইমরানের সাথে থাকে। ইমরান একজন তরুণ ডাক্তার, প্রায়ই রাতের ডিউটি করে। লম্বা যাতায়াত, রাত জাগা আর নতুন দায়িত্ব ধীরে ধীরে তার রুটিন বদলে দিচ্ছে।

units.focus: Recent changes and experiences in Tanvir's routine
units.focusBn: তানভীরের রুটিনে সাম্প্রতিক পরিবর্তন ও অভিজ্ঞতা

sessions.pattern: Subject + have / has + past participle (+ just / already / since / lately).
sessions.tipBn: অতীতের কাজের ফল এখনো আছে বোঝাতে have/has + past participle হয়; just, already, since প্রায়ই সাথে থাকে।

items.en: Tanvir has just switched off his third alarm of the morning.
He has already missed the office shuttle twice this week.
Imran has made a pot of strong tea for both of them.
Since he started this job, Tanvir has stopped going to the gym.
The traffic near Farmgate has gotten much worse lately.
He has found that podcasts make the long bus ride feel shorter.

sessions.pattern: Subject + haven't / hasn't + past participle (+ yet / since). / has never + past participle.
sessions.tipBn: না-বোধক করতে haven't/hasn't বসে; yet সাধারণত বাক্যের শেষে বসে।

items.en: Tanvir hasn't eaten a proper breakfast all week.
He hasn't been to the gym since March.
Imran hasn't slept properly because he has had three night shifts in a row.
They haven't cooked dinner at home for several days.
Tanvir has never taken a nap at his desk before.
He hasn't found time to call his parents in Sylhet yet.

sessions.pattern: Have / Has + subject + (ever / already) + past participle ...?
sessions.tipBn: প্রশ্ন করতে Have/Has শুরুতে বসে; অভিজ্ঞতা জানতে ever ব্যবহার হয়।

items.en: Have you ever woken up without an alarm clock?
Has Tanvir had anything to eat since this morning?
Has the office shuttle already left the stop?
Have you tried going to bed before midnight this week?
Has Imran finished his night shift at the hospital?
Have your working hours changed since the new manager arrived?

sessions.pattern: Wh- word + have / has + subject + past participle?
sessions.tipBn: How long, How many times ইত্যাদি দিয়ে present perfect-এ প্রশ্ন করা যায়।

items.en: How long have you lived in this flat in Mohammadpur?
What has changed most in your routine since you started working?
How many times have you been late this month?
Where have you put my phone charger, Imran?
Why has Tanvir stopped going for his morning walk?
Which new habits have you picked up since moving to Dhaka?

sessions.pattern: 3 to 4 sentences, mostly have / has + past participle.
sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে সাম্প্রতিক পরিবর্তন ও অভিজ্ঞতা বলতে বেশিরভাগ বাক্যে present perfect থাকে।

items.title: Two months in
items.en: Tanvir has worked in Gulshan for two months now, and his life has changed a lot. He has moved into a small flat with Imran and has bought his first office shirts. He has already learned the fastest bus route. However, he hasn't found time for exercise yet.

items.title: A tired flatmate
items.en: Imran has just come home from a twelve-hour night shift. He has taken off his shoes, but he hasn't changed his clothes. He has fallen asleep on the sofa with the lights on. Tanvir has covered him with a blanket and quietly closed the door.

items.title: A small victory
items.en: This week Tanvir has woken up at 6:30 every day. He has made his own breakfast three times and has even walked around the lake twice. He hasn't pressed the snooze button once. For the first time since he moved to Dhaka, he feels in control of his mornings.

units.focus: Background and interrupted actions on hectic days
units.focusBn: ব্যস্ত দিনে চলমান ও হঠাৎ বাধা পাওয়া কাজ

sessions.pattern: Subject + was / were + verb-ing (+ when / while ...).
sessions.tipBn: অতীতে কোনো কাজ চলছিল বোঝাতে was/were + verb-ing হয়; হঠাৎ ঘটা কাজটি when দিয়ে past simple-এ বসে।

items.en: Tanvir was brushing his teeth when the power went out.
While he was ironing his shirt, Imran was frying eggs.
At 8 o'clock, thousands of people were waiting at the Farmgate bus stop.
It was raining heavily, and the streets were slowly flooding.
Tanvir was answering emails on his phone during the whole ride.
When he finally reached the office, his team was already having a meeting.

sessions.tipBn: অতীতের কোনো মুহূর্তে কাজটি চলছিল না বোঝাতে wasn't/weren't + verb-ing হয়।

items.en: Tanvir wasn't paying attention when the bus reached his stop.
The air conditioner wasn't working, so everyone was sweating.
Imran wasn't sleeping when Tanvir left; he was studying for an exam.
The elevators weren't running because of the power cut.
Nobody was talking in the office when he walked in late.
He wasn't feeling hungry, so he skipped lunch again.

sessions.tipBn: প্রশ্ন করতে Was/Were বাক্যের শুরুতে বসে।

items.en: Were you sleeping when I called you at 7 o'clock?
Was it still raining when you left the office?
Was Imran working a night shift last Thursday?
Were the buses running normally after the heavy rain?
Was Tanvir listening to a podcast when his boss called?
Were your neighbors making noise while you were trying to sleep?

sessions.pattern: Wh- word + was / were + subject + verb-ing?
sessions.tipBn: Wh- শব্দের পরে was/were, তারপর subject ও verb-ing বসে।

items.en: What were you doing when the power went out?
Why was Tanvir running toward the bus stop at 7:45?
Who was Tanvir talking to on the phone during lunch?
What was Imran cooking when you came home?
Where were you going in such a hurry this morning?
Which song were you humming in the shower?

sessions.pattern: 3 to 4 sentences, mostly was / were + verb-ing.
sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে অতীতের পটভূমি বর্ণনা করতে বেশিরভাগ বাক্যে past continuous থাকে; হঠাৎ ঘটা কাজ past simple-এ।

items.title: A Monday to forget
items.en: Last Monday, everything was going wrong. Tanvir was shaving when the water stopped, and Imran was shouting about a missing sock. Outside, it was raining heavily and horns were blaring on every street. By the time a rickshaw stopped, Tanvir was already running late.

items.title: Stuck in traffic
items.en: At six in the evening, Tanvir's bus was crawling along Bijoy Sarani. Some passengers were sleeping, and others were scrolling through their phones. A young man was selling cucumbers and peanuts between the cars. Tanvir was watching the sunset and thinking about dinner.

items.title: A late-night talk
items.en: When Imran came home at midnight, Tanvir was still sitting at his laptop. He was finishing a report while his tea was getting cold. Imran was feeling too tired to sleep, so they talked about their routines. Soon they were both laughing at old stories from their school days.

units.focus: Advice, rules and possibilities for a healthier routine
units.focusBn: স্বাস্থ্যকর রুটিনের জন্য পরামর্শ, নিয়ম ও সম্ভাবনা

sessions.pattern: Subject + should / must / have to / might / could / need to + verb (base).
sessions.tipBn: should পরামর্শ, must ও have to বাধ্যবাধকতা, might সম্ভাবনা বোঝায়; এদের পরে verb মূল রূপে বসে।

items.en: You should put away your phone an hour before bed.
Tanvir has to be at his desk by 9 o'clock sharp.
We must switch off the gas before we leave the flat.
Imran might sleep until noon after his night shift.
You could take the metro instead of the bus.
I need to buy a new alarm clock this weekend.

sessions.pattern: Subject + shouldn't / mustn't / can't / might not / don't have to / don't need to + verb (base).
sessions.tipBn: mustn't মানে কাজটি করা নিষেধ, কিন্তু don't have to মানে করার দরকার নেই।

items.en: You shouldn't drink coffee late in the evening.
Tanvir doesn't have to go to the office on Fridays.
You mustn't leave the iron on when you go out.
Imran can't sleep well when the neighbors are playing loud music.
We don't need to cook tonight; there's leftover rice and curry.
You might not get a seat on the 8 o'clock bus.

sessions.pattern: Should / Can / Could / May + subject + verb (base) ...? / Do + subject + have to ...?
sessions.tipBn: modal-এর প্রশ্নে modal শুরুতে বসে; have to-এর প্রশ্নে Do বা Does লাগে।

items.en: Should I wake you up before I leave for work?
Do we have to pay the electricity bill this week?
Can you pick up some bread on your way home?
Could I leave work a little early on Thursday?
Should Tanvir see a doctor about his back pain?
May I use your charger for a few minutes?

sessions.tipBn: বাক্য হ্যাঁ-বোধক হলে ট্যাগ না-বোধক হয়, আর বাক্য না-বোধক হলে ট্যাগ হ্যাঁ-বোধক হয়।

items.en: You should go to bed earlier, shouldn't you?
We have to leave by 7:30 tomorrow, don't we?
Imran can't take a day off this week, can he?
You mustn't forget your ID card again, must you?
I shouldn't skip breakfast every day, should I?
We could walk to the lake this evening, couldn't we?

sessions.pattern: 3 to 4 sentences with should / must / have to / might / could / need to.
sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে পরামর্শ, নিয়ম ও সম্ভাবনা বোঝাতে বিভিন্ন modal ব্যবহার হয়।

items.title: Imran's advice
items.en: Imran says Tanvir must take his health more seriously. He should sleep at least seven hours and shouldn't eat heavy food late at night. He could also try a short walk after dinner. Most importantly, he needs to stop checking emails in bed.

items.title: Office rules
items.en: At Tanvir's company, employees have to scan their ID cards when they arrive. They don't have to wear formal clothes, but they must attend the ten o'clock meeting. Staff may work from home on Thursdays if their manager agrees. Tanvir thinks these rules are fair.

items.title: A plan for Friday
items.en: Tomorrow is Friday, so Tanvir doesn't have to set an alarm. He might sleep late, or he could go to the market with Imran. In the afternoon, he must call his parents because he promised. He should also do his laundry before the new week starts.

units.focus: Real and imagined changes to Tanvir's routine
units.focusBn: তানভীরের রুটিনে বাস্তব ও কাল্পনিক পরিবর্তন

sessions.pattern: If + present simple, will + verb. / If + past simple, would + verb.
sessions.tipBn: সম্ভব ঘটনায় If + present, will; আর কল্পনার ঘটনায় If + past, would ব্যবহার হয়।

items.en: If Tanvir leaves home at 7 o'clock, he will beat the worst traffic.
If it rains tomorrow, I'll take a taxi instead of the bus.
If I lived closer to the office, I would walk to work.
If Imran had a day job, we would eat dinner together every night.
If you go to bed now, you'll feel fresh in the morning.
I would exercise every morning if I had more energy.

sessions.pattern: If + don't / didn't ..., won't / wouldn't + verb.
sessions.tipBn: শর্তবাক্যের যেকোনো অংশ না-বোধক হতে পারে: don't/didn't অথবা won't/wouldn't।

items.en: If you don't set two alarms, you won't wake up in time.
If Tanvir didn't work so late, he wouldn't feel so exhausted.
I won't have time for breakfast if I sleep another ten minutes.
If I were you, I wouldn't check my phone first thing in the morning.
If the power doesn't come back soon, the food in the fridge won't stay fresh.
Imran wouldn't be so tired if he didn't have night shifts.

sessions.pattern: Wh- word + will / would + subject + verb + if ...?
sessions.tipBn: Wh- প্রশ্নের সাথে if-অংশ যোগ করে শর্তের ফল জানতে চাওয়া হয়।

items.en: What will you do if you miss the last bus?
Where would you live if you could choose any area of Dhaka?
How will you get home if the roads flood again?
What would you change about your routine if you had more free time?
Who will cook dinner if both of you come home late?
How would you feel if you could sleep until noon every day?

sessions.pattern: 3 to 4 sentences with if-clauses (first and second conditional).
sessions.tipBn: অনুচ্ছেদে সম্ভব পরিকল্পনার জন্য first conditional আর কল্পনার জন্য second conditional ব্যবহার হয়।

items.title: The five o'clock plan
items.en: If Tanvir wakes up at five o'clock, he will have time for a walk around the lake. If he walks every day, he will sleep better at night. And if he sleeps better, he won't feel so sleepy in afternoon meetings. It sounds simple, but will he really do it?

items.title: Dreaming of a short commute
items.en: Tanvir spends almost three hours a day in traffic. If he lived in Gulshan, he would walk to work in ten minutes. He would use the extra time to cook, read and exercise. But rent in Gulshan is very high, so he would need a much bigger salary.

items.title: Imran's dream
items.en: Imran sometimes imagines a different life. If he didn't work night shifts, he would have breakfast with Tanvir every morning. If he had weekends off, he would visit his family in Rajshahi more often. For now, he sleeps whenever he can.
